column37: This restriction type refers to account deletion. Any account, regardless of privacy settings, may be deleted for violating Flickr's T&C. When an account is deleted, all associated content, including photos, albums, and group contributions, is removed from the platform. The account holder can no longer access their content, and the account will no longer appear in search results or via existing links. This restriction type also covers account deletions imposed where a user frequently provides illegal content or repeatedly violates Flickr's policies.

column5: Sexualization of minors. Includes exploitive or sexualizing content or conduct that does not rise to the level of illegality.
Child nudity. While child nudity is permitted on Flickr provided it is not sexualizing or exploitive in any way (e.g., birthing photos, etc.), it must be non-public.
Compromised accounts have visibility restricted pending approval from verified owner

Risky signup. Flickr automatically prevents the creation of new accounts from users suspected of engaging in prohibited spam or fraud activity, based on rules-based automated evaluation workflows (via third-party Sift).
Risky engagement. Flickr closes accounts of users engaging in prohibited spam or fraud activity, based on rules-based automated evaluation workflows (via third-party Sift).
Explicit video. Sexually explicit videos are prohibited.
Improperly moderated. Content that the user has failed to assign the proper safety levels to.
NSFW on Free Account. Adult themes, including nudity and sexual content, are permitted only on paid subscriber accounts.
Commercial activity. Commercial activities are permitted only on paid subscriber accounts.
